surprise.title: FSU and Florida meet for the 70th time today, in a series a governor had to talk into existence
surprise.body: When Florida State restarted football in 1947, Florida's administration refused to schedule the Seminoles, partly out of worry that treating FSU as an equal would cost UF state funding as the flagship. A 1955 bill in the Florida Legislature would have forced the two schools to play, and it failed, so Governor LeRoy Collins personally asked UF president J. Wayne Reitz to start a yearly series. The first game came on November 22, 1958, a 21 to 7 Florida win, and the contract required the first six games to be played in Gainesville because Doak Campbell held fewer than 20,000 people. Tallahassee has hosted every other year since 1964 after FSU kept expanding the stadium. Florida dominated early, including a 49 to 0 game in 1973 and nine straight wins from 1968 to 1976, until Bobby Bowden arrived in 1976 and made it a real fight. From 1990 to 2001 both teams entered every meeting ranked in the top ten. Florida leads the series 39-28-2 and has won the last two, yet the games played in Tallahassee are dead even at 14-14-1, so a home win today breaks the tie. Kickoff is 3:30 PM at Doak; the forecast is dry, about 57 degrees at kickoff, cooling to around 52 by 6 PM after a 5:36 PM sunset. Sixteen days until you sail on December 13.
